problem: What evidence is sufficient to refine a partial-order institutional history into an authoritative precedence relation?
candidateLaw: Occurrence/arrival/timestamp evidence does not become institutional precedence merely by existing or being authentic; precedence requires an admitted ordering policy/witness for the relevant institutional claim scope.

witnessArms.NO_WITNESS: all unique permutations of the concurrent batch remain admissible
witnessArms.ARRIVAL_ONLY: a recorded arrival order is supplied but explicitly has no authority role; admissible set must not shrink
witnessArms.AUTHENTIC_NONADMITTED: the order evidence is authentic, but current institutional policy does not admit that evidence role for precedence; admissible set must not shrink
witnessArms.ADMITTED_PRECEDENCE: an authenticated order witness is admitted by current policy for this event scope; admissible executions are filtered to orders consistent with the witness

targetedRaces: the nine S5B-A targeted concurrent races
properties: ARRIVAL_ONLY preserves the no-witness binding/continuation sets
AUTHENTIC_NONADMITTED preserves the no-witness binding/continuation sets
ADMITTED_PRECEDENCE selects exactly the witnessed linearization in the two-event targeted races
admitted order may remove ambiguity but does not guarantee the selected resulting state is safe for consequential action
guards: S6A is a checker-layer experiment; it does not add a new global clock/order truth owner.
The selected witness order is one already admissible linearization; S6A does not permit a witness to contradict known happened-before constraints.
Institutional precedence policy is scope/role-relative, consistent with existing Interlocus authority-policy/currentness theory.
